entries.title: II Kings 25:3
segments: No human power or skill can avail against the providence of God; and when he undertakes to punish guilty individuals or nations, without repentance and reformation there is no escape.

entries.title: II Kings 25:4
segments: Between two walls--by the king's garden; this gate was in the southern part of the city, near the pool of Siloam,
.  The double wall here mentioned was probably built across the valley that lies between Zion adn Ophel, at the mouth of which valley is the pool of Siloam.

entries.title: II Kings 25:5
segments: The plains of Jericho; the deep valley through which the Jordan lows and in which the Dead sea lies.

entries.title: II Kings 25:7
segments: The obstinate wickedness of parents is often the occasion of ruin to their children; and those senses which have been inlets of iniquity, become inlets of torment.

entries.title: II Kings 25:9
segments: As a punishment to his people, the Lord sometimes suffers the wicked to abolish the observance of his own ordinances, and to carry away or destroy what has been most solemnly devoted to his service.

entries.title: II Kings 25:10
segments: Brake down the walls; to prevent the inhabitants of Jerusalem from giving the king of Babylon any further trouble.

entries.title: II Kings 25:16
segments: The two pillars--sea--bases; see the description of these in

. 
 
  Without weight; in such abundance, that the quantity and its value were not estimated.

entries.title: II Kings 25:18
segments: Those most intimately associated with the wicked in crime, are most exposed to be partakers with them in punishment.

entries.title: II Kings 25:21
segments: Slew them at Riblah; as special friends of Zedekiah and men of influence among the people.

entries.title: II Kings 25:24
segments: Supreme power is often greatly coveted, and no crimes are so base as not to be perpetrated to obtain it.  But the greater the power which is obtained by iniquity, the greater curse it will be to those who receive it.

entries.title: II Kings 25:25
segments: Mizpah; supposed to be a town in the tribe of Benjamin.

entries.title: II Kings 25:27
segments: The hearts of kings, and of all others, are in the hands of the Lord; and he can at any time incline them to favor even the most abject and distressed, and thus show them and others that they who truly seek the Lord shall not want any good thing.

entries.title: II Kings 25:28
segments: The kings; those who had been conquered by the Babylonians, and who were kept as prisoners at Babylon.
